newsitem.title: USA: McCurry defends Dole aide on drug issue.
newsitem.headline: McCurry defends Dole aide on drug issue.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Wednesday that Dole campaign aide John Buckley had been "done an injustice" by reports that Buckley used marijuana in college.

"Having been in that situation and considering him a personal friend, I think he's been done an injustice," said McCurry, who himself came under fire in July after admitting he occasionally smoked "a joint" as a student in the 1970s.
McCurry said he did not doubt "for a moment" that Buckley believes "whatever he did in college was wrong just as I believe what I did in college was wrong."

"We have to all work together, Republican and Democrat, to send a message that drug use can kill you. I'm sure that John Buckley believes that, and if he had an opportunity, he would say that," McCurry said.

Buckley, the Dole campaign communications director, has refused to confirm or deny reports allegations that he used small amounts of marijuana while a student at Hampshire College in Massachussetts in the late 1970s.
He claims the issue is no longer "relevant" and says he supports Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole's campaign against drug use.
